title: Tôi không muốn bất kỳ rắc rối nào
englishTitle: I do not want any trouble
pronunciation: Toi khong muon bat ky rac roi nao
summary: I do not want any trouble

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Tôi không muốn bất kỳ rắc rối nào explains a limit without making the exchange tense. It helps someone understand I do not want any trouble and offer a simpler option, a written detail, or a next step.

sections.title: Quick say
sections.body: Say Tôi không muốn bất kỳ rắc rối nào calmly and show the proof if you have it: phone screen, address, document, visible problem, or nearby staff member. After that, let the other person ask one follow-up or point you to the right next step.

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: Nearby follow-ups: Call the police, Call an ambulance, and I lost my passport.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Best at a hotel desk, during a street help moment, or at a police counter, before the explanation gets long. Keep the location, passport copy, photo, injury, or helper contact close for the follow-up.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Keep the explanation simple and show the evidence if you can. A short phrase plus a photo, receipt, or booking usually works better than adding more English.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: These follow-ups cover location, documents, help, or reporting: I feel unsafe, This is an emergency, and Help!
